title: Fix an inherited PuLP valve replacement model

blocks.text: A gas utility inherited `valves.py`, a PuLP script that picks which valves to replace this year. It runs every night without an error, and every night it reports `Optimal`. The planners have stopped trusting it: it once proposed more crew-weeks than the utility has, it has dropped valves that last year's plan funded, it left the harbor district below its agreed share, and once it returned a plan for a year when the rules could not all be met.

Fix `plan(valves, budget, crew_weeks, harbor_band, last_year)` so that it returns the plan the formulation below defines, as `(risk cut, sorted valve ids)`, or `None` when no plan meets every rule. The function's shape stays: same arguments, same return.

With $`V`$ the valves, $`V_H \subseteq V`$ those in the harbor district, and $`L \subseteq V`$ the valves `last_year` marks with 1. Each valve $`i`$ cuts risk by $`r_i`$ ($k a year), costs $`c_i`$ ($k) and takes $`w_i`$ crew-weeks. The year has a budget $`B`$, $`W`$ crew-weeks, and a harbor band from $`\ell`$ to $`u`$ ($k).

\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \sum_{i \in V} r_i\, z_i && && \text{(risk\_cut)} \\
& \sum_{i \in V} c_i\, z_i \le B && && \text{(budget)} \\
& \sum_{i \in V} w_i\, z_i \le W && && \text{(crew)} \\
& \ell \le \sum_{i \in V_H} c_i\, z_i \le u && && \text{(harbor)} \\
& z_i = 1 && \forall i \in L && \text{(lock}_i) \\
& z_i \in \{0, 1\} && \forall i \in V
\end{aligned}

Every line of the script runs, so look for lines that do not mean what they say. The tests run the script on small cases you could solve by hand. The reference changes five lines, counting the import it extends with `LpStatusOptimal`. One of them becomes two rows: the reference writes the harbor band as `harbor_min` ($`\sum_{i \in V_H} c_i z_i \ge \ell`$) and `harbor_max` ($`\sum_{i \in V_H} c_i z_i \le u`$).

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from pulp import PULP_CBC_CMD, LpMaximize, LpProblem, LpStatusOptimal, LpVariable, lpSum, value


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Valve:
    vid: str
    district: str
    risk_cut: float       # expected leak cost avoided a year, $k
    cost: float           # replacement cost, $k
    crew_weeks: int


def plan(valves, budget, crew_weeks, harbor_band, last_year):
    """The best replacement plan as (risk cut, sorted valve ids), or None when no plan exists."""
    z = LpVariable.dicts("z", [v.vid for v in valves], cat="Binary")
    prob = LpProblem("valves", LpMaximize)
    prob += lpSum(v.risk_cut * z[v.vid] for v in valves), "risk_cut"

    prob += lpSum(v.cost * z[v.vid] for v in valves) <= budget, "budget"
    prob += lpSum(v.crew_weeks * z[v.vid] for v in valves) <= crew_weeks, "crew"

    lo, hi = harbor_band
    harbor = lpSum(v.cost * z[v.vid] for v in valves if v.district == "harbor")
    prob += harbor >= lo, "harbor_min"
    prob += harbor <= hi, "harbor_max"

    for vid, was_funded in last_year.items():
        if was_funded == 1:
            prob += z[vid] == 1, "lock_" + vid

    status = prob.solve(PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=0, gapRel=0))
    if status != LpStatusOptimal:
        return None
    return value(prob.objective), sorted(vid for vid in z if value(z[vid]) > 0.5)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo = [Valve("H1", "harbor", 30, 40, 3), Valve("U1", "uptown", 25, 20, 4)]
    print(plan(demo, budget=60, crew_weeks=7, harbor_band=(0, 100), last_year={}))

cases.says: with crew-weeks the binding limit, the plan cuts the most risk that fits the crews and the budget
with crews to spare, the plan cuts the most risk the budget can buy
every valve funded last year is in this year's plan, even when another plan would cut more risk
the harbor district receives at least the low end of its band
when the rules cannot all hold, the function says there is no plan instead of returning one

origin.section: Read `status` and `sol_status` Before Any Value, and Expect None

concepts: older PuLP code makes variables with LpVariable.dicts, sets the objective with an unnamed +=, and reads answers through LpStatus, varValue and value
a result is read only after both status codes say there is a plan, and a variable outside the problem has no value
a bool handed to += is dropped or refused, a chained band keeps its right half, and an expression replaces the objective
